problem: The existing bounded activation-steering search used sign-paired target intervention and a physical zero-vector no-op, but could still accept a direction when any same-magnitude nonzero activation perturbation produced the same score gain.
hypothesis: A genuine direction-specific search signal should beat equal-L2-norm random-direction perturbations at the same selected layer, alpha and seeds.
counterhypothesis: The apparent steering gain is generic perturbation sensitivity rather than specificity of the decoded J-Space control direction.

external_research_input.source_claim_used: Causal activation-steering evaluation can compare learned intervention directions with equal-magnitude random perturbations and inspect layerwise intervention sensitivity.

implemented_discriminator.name: EQUAL_L2_NORM_RANDOM_DIRECTION_CONTROL
requirements: same L2 norm within explicit tolerance
not target direction or its sign inverse
executor hook receipt must bind exact applied random-vector SHA-256
implemented_discriminator.success_gate: target mean delta must exceed the maximum absolute mean delta of all supplied equal-norm random controls by min_random_specificity_gap

synthetic_regression_definition.positive_case: target vector (1,0) on synthetic target axis with equal-norm random vector (0,1) keeps target-specific gain and zero random mean delta
synthetic_regression_definition.negative_case: executor where every nonzero perturbation gets the same gain must fail because target and equal-norm random control have equal mean delta

execution_evidence.note: Source and regression definitions are durable, but no exact-branch test execution was observed in this macrocycle.
